questions.def: 'Fell through' means the plan failed to happen.
questions.question: The meeting fell ___ due to the manager's illness.

questions.def: 'Ran into' means to meet someone unexpectedly.
questions.question: I ___ my old school friend in the supermarket yesterday.

questions.def: Should be 'She takes after her mother' or 'She is taking after her mother'
questions.question: She takes after her mother, who also loves to sing.

questions.def: 'Look over' means to examine something carefully.
questions.question: We need to ___ the contract carefully before signing.

questions.def: 'Cut down on' means to reduce the amount of something.
questions.question: The company is trying to cut ___ on its expenses.

questions.def: 'Got over' means to overcome a problem or difficulty.
questions.question: He ___ his shyness and gave a great speech.

questions.def: 'Bring about' means to cause something to happen.
questions.question: The new policy is meant to ___ positive change.

questions.def: 'Call off' means to cancel something.
questions.question: They called ___ the meeting due to lack of interest.

questions.def: 'Come in for' means to receive something, often criticism.
questions.question: She ___ a lot of criticism for her controversial remarks.

questions.def: 'Get on with' means to continue doing something.
questions.question: It's time to ___ with your work.

questions.def: 'Ran out of' means to have no more of something.
questions.question: The company ran ___ of money and had to close.

questions.def: 'Spread out' means to extend over a wide area.
questions.question: The fire ___ quickly, causing extensive damage.

questions.def: 'Turn down' means to reject an offer or proposal.
questions.question: The company decided to ___ his offer.

questions.def: 'Came into' means to inherit something.
questions.question: She came ___ a lot of money after her grandfather died.

questions.def: 'Went over' means to review or explain something.
questions.question: The teacher ___ the homework assignment.

questions.def: 'Sort out' means to resolve a problem or difficulty.
questions.question: We need to ___ the problem as soon as possible.

questions.def: 'Hold out' means to have a small amount of hope.
questions.question: I don't hold ___ much hope for their success.

questions.def: 'Bringing out' means to launch or release something.
questions.question: The company is ___ a new product next month.

questions.def: 'Broke down' means to fail or collapse.
questions.question: The negotiations ___ after hours of disagreement.

questions.def: 'Back out' means to withdraw from an agreement.
questions.question: He backed ___ of the deal at the last minute.

questions.def: 'Drew up' means to attract or gain.
questions.question: The noise ___ my attention.

questions.def: 'Play out' can mean to perform a role effectively.
questions.question: He ___ his role perfectly in the play.

questions.def: 'Come out' means to become known or revealed.
questions.question: The truth will come ___ eventually.

questions.def: 'Go through' means to examine or review something carefully.
questions.question: I need to ___ my notes before the exam.

questions.def: "Fall through" means to fail to happen.
questions.question: The meeting fell ___ because of the storm.

questions.def: "Get across" means to communicate effectively.
questions.question: She struggled to get her point ___ in the debate.

questions.def: "Break down" (negotiations) means to fail.
questions.question: Negotiations ___ after several hours.

questions.def: "Roll out" means to launch or introduce.
questions.question: The company plans to roll ___ the new software next month.

questions.def: "Bring down" means to cause to fall from power.
questions.question: The scandal brought ___ the government.

questions.def: "Carry out" means to execute or perform.
questions.question: They ___ their threats.
